E3 supports parabolic kinetics and Al2O3/Cr2O3 formation but does not address Mn. E1 is about spinel ferrites for batteries and is irrelevant to high-temperature oxidation of bulk HEAs. premises: Al or Si forms a slow-growing, thermodynamically stable, adherent, coherent oxide scale (Al2O3 or silica) that limits oxygen ingress and suppresses internal stresses.
Mn forms less stable, faster-growing, less coherent oxides that generate higher internal stresses and are prone to cracking/spallation.
The nature of the oxide scale (coherence, adhesion, growth rate) is governed by the distribution and local enrichment of the oxide-forming element at the alloy surface.
The intervention modulates oxidation behavior by controlling the kinetics of outward metal diffusion versus inward oxygen diffusion.
Parabolic oxidation kinetics are typical for diffusion-controlled processes, and Al2O3 scales grow slower than chromium oxide scales and are more stable.
